items.title: AI helps narrow experience gap between mammography readers
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: researchers will report whether AI-assisted mammography improves diagnostic performance differently for junior and senior readers and whether it narrows experience-related performance gaps.

items.title: AI linked to higher recall rates in screening mammography
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: real-world results from a tertiary cancer center comparing screening mammography interpretations with and without AI, finding AI use associated with higher recall rates.

items.title: DL risk model outperforms clinical assessment at safety net hospital
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: performance of the Mirai deep-learning breast cancer risk model at a diverse urban safety-net hospital, outperforming traditional clinical risk assessment.

items.title: AI improves rare kidney cancer diagnosis, but overreliance poses risks: AMC study
items.excerpt: Asan Medical Center's deep-learning tool raised 21 pathologists' accuracy in diagnosing fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma from 60.0% to 73.3%, but physicians who relied more on it were more likely to accept its wrong calls.

items.title: Samsung, OpenAI push connected healthcare in US as Korea faces data barriers
items.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and OpenAI are expanding services that connect personal health data with U.S. hospitals for clinical use, while fragmented hospital information systems and weak interoperability hold Korea back.

items.title: Patient comfort with AI's clinical decisions tied to provider oversight: Gallup
items.excerpt: A new Gallup poll finds patients are more open to AI making decisions about their care than providers assume, but human oversight is what makes them comfortable with it.

items.title: AI-derived inflammation score improves cardiovascular risk prediction beyond CAC
items.excerpt: A JAMA analysis from Oxford finds an AI-derived coronary inflammation score from noncontrast CT flags elevated cardiovascular risk even when calcium scores are zero, performing comparably to CCTA measures.

items.title: Multicenter benchmarking of large language models for bladder cancer management recommendations from mpMRI reports
items.excerpt: Following TRIPOD-LLM, researchers retrospectively tested nine API-accessed LLMs on 590 bladder cancer mpMRI reports across centers to see whether they generate guideline-concordant management recommendations.

items.title: Beyond skin deep: physiologic oral pigmentation as an overlooked validation gap in AI-assisted oral cancer screening
items.excerpt: AI oral cancer screening tools such as MeMoSA were validated almost only in Asian populations; the authors argue physiologic oral pigmentation, which varies by race, may cause classifiers to flag normal variation as suspicious.

items.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model to predict the daily risk of febrile neutropenia in patients with AML undergoing chemotherapy
items.excerpt: Using registry data from two Finnish university hospital districts, researchers trained and validated an AI model that predicts the daily risk of febrile neutropenia in acute myeloid leukemia patients during chemotherapy.

items.title: Beyond the Rogue Agent—Preparing Health Systems for AI Failure
items.excerpt: JAMA Viewpoint on how health systems should prepare for, and stay resilient through, failures of AI embedded in clinical operations (date via Crossref created, DOI 10.1001/jama.2026.24040).

items.title: AI chatbots aren't therapists. But can they finally get men to open up?
items.excerpt: STAT examines whether AI chatbots, though imperfect therapists, can lower the barriers that keep men from seeking mental health care.

items.title: AMA: Artificial intelligence can augment physicians but don't call it doctor
items.excerpt: At its 2026 Interim Meeting the AMA adopted policy that AI cannot be granted licensure or professional titles to practice medicine, and called for laws shielding physicians from liability when AI products fail and requiring vendors to disclose failure rates. (Off-list: on-list coverage only inside a Fierce Healthcare roundup.)

items.title: Weekly Rundown: Ohio State Wexner, Microsoft ink tech deal; OpenEvidence launches free Access Intelligence tools
items.excerpt: Weekly health AI brief for Nov. 9-13: OpenEvidence's free Access Intelligence tools for clinicians, R1's agentic Phare Auth/UM/Denials modules, Microsoft-Ohio State Wexner smart hospital deal, and the AMA's AI licensure policy.

items.title: NHS launches £200k project to shape how safety and performance of AI diagnostic tools are monitored
items.excerpt: The NHS has asked the Royal College of Radiologists to lead a discovery exercise on post-deployment monitoring of AI diagnostic tools, covering current challenges, bias and needed governance. (Off-list: gov.uk / england.nhs.uk had no item.)

items.title: Insilico's AI-designed TEAD inhibitor shrank tumors in 4 of 22 mesothelioma patients; randomized Phase 2a planned for 2027
items.excerpt: Insilico Medicine's AI-designed pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331 produced responses in 4 of 22 pretreated mesothelioma patients in early clinical data; a randomized Phase 2a is planned for 2027. (Off-list: endpts/fiercebiotech unreachable.)

items.title: FDA Clears IND for Biolojic's BD200, the First AI-Designed Multibody ADC to Enter Clinical Trials
items.excerpt: FDA cleared Biolojic Design's IND for BD200, an AI-designed Trop2/Nectin-4 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate whose arms can each bind either target; a global Phase 1 in solid tumors starts within weeks. (Off-list: on-list biotech feeds had no coverage.)
